# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick is the JBL Charge 6.** Several reviewers rate it highly and it suits both settings.

## Top picks

- **Best overall: JBL Charge 6** (about $130-$150)
  - It has an IP68 rating, so it is sealed against sand and dust and can survive submersion.
  - Battery life is 20 hours, or 28 with Playtime Boost, and it can charge your phone. What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and BestProducts did too.
  - BestProducts listed it at $150 (25% off $200), and What Hi-Fi listed it at $129.99 at Walmart.
  - [What Hi-Fi review and deals](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) · [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

- **Best for pool parties: JBL Boombox 4**
  - RTINGS named it the best waterproof speaker it has tested. It floats, handles long immersion, gets loud, and lasts over 40 hours.
  - Its sound is directional and can get muffled if you're beside or behind it. It's also big and pricey, and I didn't see a price in the results.
  - [RTINGS review and buy links](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

- **Best 360° sound: Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM** (IP67)
  - It floats, sounds the same from any side, and lasts about 15 hours. Tom's Guide ranked it best overall and RTINGS ranked it best mid-range.
  - [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) · [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

- **Best for carrying to the beach: JBL Grip** (about $100, IP68)
  - It's the size of a drink can and weighs under a pound. A Good Housekeeping DJ tester found it loud enough for a 30+ person party. The mesh body can trap dust.
  - [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)

## Cheaper options

- **Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4** (about $65 on sale, IP67): It floats, has 360° sound and lasts 14 hours. [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **JBL Go 5** ($39.95, IP67): It's soap-sized, but battery life is only about 8 hours. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)
- **Soundcore Boom 2** (about $110 on sale): It floats and has strong bass, but no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach. [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

## If you want something louder

The **Soundcore Boom 2 Plus** is a 100 W floating speaker rated IPX7, with up to 20 hours of battery at half volume. It's heavy at 3.8 kg and has no dust rating. Dealectric says code AFSC20 takes $49.99 off the $249.99 price, for $200. That is a third-party claim, and the checkout has the final word. [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus) (an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you).

## Care tips

IP ratings don't cover corrosion from salt or chlorine. RTINGS recommends rinsing the speaker with fresh water after use. Check your model's manual first, since some advise against beach or shower use. Keep the charging port closed, and dry the speaker completely before charging.

For a beach and pool all-rounder, I'd go with the Charge 6. Tell me your budget and group size and I can narrow it down.
